# Pawpath Online Rebooking

**Author:** [account name from CLI context] | **Date:** 2026-10-15 | **Status:** Draft v1.0

Pawpath Online Rebooking enables pet owners to confirm a follow-up visit in one tap directly from an SMS or email reminder, eliminating the phone-call barrier that causes 31% of recheck patients to fall through. By surfacing a pre-populated booking link tied to the existing Pawpath calendar service, the feature targets an increase in the recheck rebooking rate from 69% to 80% within two quarters and a reduction in clinic reminder-call labor from 6 to 2 hours per week — without touching payment flows or requiring calendar infrastructure changes.

---

## Problem Statement

Three compounding problems erode clinic revenue and staff efficiency:

- **Patient dropout:** 31% of pets due for a recheck never rebook, representing a direct gap in continuity of care and clinic revenue.
- **Friction at the point of intent:** Rebooking today requires a phone call. Because 74% of owners open Pawpath reminders on a phone, they are ready to act but hit a dead end when no self-service option exists.
- **Staff burden:** Front-desk teams spend approximately 6 hours per week per clinic on manual reminder calls — time that could be redirected to in-clinic care.

**Gap identified:** The PM's data does not yet quantify the revenue impact per lost recheck. Before launch, the team should calculate average revenue per recheck visit to model the full business case and prioritize pilot clinic selection.

---

## Target Users & Personas

### Persona 1 — Maya, Pet Owner (Primary)
- **Context:** Received a reminder that her dog Biscuit's 2-week post-surgery recheck is due. She's at work, opens the SMS on her phone.
- **Pain:** Has to call the clinic during business hours; forgets by the time she's free.
- **Need:** Book the appointment in under 60 seconds without a phone call.

### Persona 2 — Jordan, Front-Desk Coordinator (Secondary)
- **Context:** Works at an independent clinic with 4 vets. Spends Monday mornings calling recheck no-shows.
- **Pain:** Reminder calls are repetitive, frequently go to voicemail, and pull focus from walk-ins.
- **Need:** Automated rebooking that reduces the call list and surfaces only truly unreachable owners.

---

## Goals & Success Metrics

| Goal | Metric | Baseline | Target | Window |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Increase rebooking rate | % of due-recheck patients who book | 69% | 80% | 2 quarters post-launch |
| Reduce staff call burden | Reminder-call hours per clinic per week | 6 hrs | 2 hrs | 2 quarters post-launch |
| Drive self-service adoption | % of new recheck bookings via online link | 0% | Target: 60% | End of beta (Week 10) |
| Maintain booking completion | Drop-off rate within the rebooking flow | — | Target: <20% | Beta period |

> **Note:** The 60% self-service adoption and <20% drop-off are targets introduced by this PRD; validate against pilot data.

---

## Requirements

### Functional Requirements

**F1 — Reminder Link Generation**
- System auto-generates a unique, pre-authenticated rebooking URL per patient per due recheck.
- Link is embedded in both SMS and email reminders sent via existing Pawpath notification pipeline.
- Link expires after the recheck due date passes (exact window: TBD with clinical ops).

**F2 — One-Tap Booking Flow**
- Tapping the link opens a mobile-optimized page pre-populated with: patient name, recheck type, and clinic location.
- Owner selects from available slots surfaced by the existing Pawpath calendar service (read/write API).
- Confirmation delivered via SMS and email within 60 seconds of booking.

**F3 — Slot Availability**
- Available slots reflect real-time calendar state; no double-booking.
- If no slots are available within a configurable look-ahead window (Assumption: 14 days default), owner is shown a "call us" fallback with the clinic phone number.

**F4 — Clinic Dashboard View**
- Front-desk staff see a "Pending Recheck" worklist filtered by: not yet rebooked, reminder sent, link not clicked, link clicked but not booked.
- Staff can mark a patient as "contacted" or "declined recheck" to remove from call list.

**F5 — Automated Reminder Cadence**
- Initial reminder: configurable days before due date (Assumption: 7 days default).
- One follow-up reminder if no booking after 3 days (configurable per clinic).
- No further automated outreach after 2 reminders; residual cases go to staff worklist.

### Non-Functional Requirements

- **Performance:** Rebooking page must load in <3 seconds on a 4G connection.
- **Availability:** Target: 99.5% uptime during clinic hours (8 am–7 pm local).
- **Security:** Pre-authenticated URLs must use signed tokens (HMAC or equivalent); tokens must not expose patient PII in the URL string.
- **Accessibility:** WCAG 2.1 AA compliance for the rebooking page.
- **Scalability:** Must support 12 pilot clinics at beta; architecture should not require re-platforming to reach Assumption: 200 clinics at general availability.

---

## User Stories & Acceptance Criteria

**US-1 — Owner books from SMS**
*As a pet owner, I want to tap a link in my SMS reminder and book a slot without calling, so I can complete the task in under 2 minutes.*
- **AC1:** Link opens rebooking page with patient name and recheck type pre-filled.
- **AC2:** Available slots display within 3 seconds.
- **AC3:** Booking confirmed; owner receives SMS confirmation within 60 seconds.
- **AC4:** Slot is blocked in the clinic calendar immediately upon confirmation.

**US-2 — Staff views worklist**
*As a front-desk coordinator, I want to see which recheck patients haven't self-booked, so I know exactly who to call.*
- **AC1:** Worklist filters to: reminder sent + no booking after 3 days.
- **AC2:** Staff can dismiss a record with a reason code (contacted, declined, already booked externally).
- **AC3:** Dismissed records are excluded from worklist and do not receive further automated reminders.

**US-3 — No slots available fallback**
*As a pet owner, I want to be directed to call the clinic if no online slots are available, so I'm not left stranded.*
- **AC1:** If zero slots exist in the look-ahead window, page displays clinic phone number prominently.
- **AC2:** Event is logged so staff worklist flags this owner as "needs manual scheduling."

---

## Scope

### In Scope
- One-tap rebooking flow accessible via SMS and email reminder links
- Mobile-optimized rebooking UI (responsive web; no new native app build)
- Integration with existing Pawpath calendar service (read/write)
- Automated 2-reminder cadence
- Front-desk worklist in existing Pawpath clinic dashboard
- Signed-token URL generation and validation

### Out of Scope
- Payment collection or deposit capture
- New calendar infrastructure (must reuse existing service)
- New appointment types beyond rechecks
- Native iOS/Android app changes
- Multi-location clinic support (Assumption: single-location clinics only at beta)

---

## Technical Considerations

- **Calendar API:** Confirm existing Pawpath calendar service exposes a write endpoint for slot reservation; if read-only today, this is a blocking dependency requiring early resolution.
- **Token security:** Signed URLs must enforce expiry and single-use or rate-limited use to prevent link forwarding abuse.
- **SMS provider:** Reuse existing Pawpath SMS pipeline; confirm character limits support a tracking URL without truncation.
- **Deep-link routing:** If owner has the Pawpath app installed, evaluate whether the link should open the app or always open a mobile web page (recommended: mobile web for lowest friction at beta).
- **Gap — data model:** Confirm the existing schema tracks "recheck due date" per visit. If not, a migration or new field is required before F1 can be built.

---

## Risks & Mitigations

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Calendar API is read-only; write not available | Medium | High | Audit API in Week 1; escalate as P0 blocker if confirmed |
| Low link click-through rate reduces impact | Medium | High | A/B test SMS copy in pilot; measure open-to-click rate weekly |
| Clinic staff don't adopt worklist, revert to full call lists | Medium | Medium | Include worklist in onboarding for all 12 pilot clinics; track adoption |
| Signed URL tokens expire before owner acts | Low | Medium | Set expiry relative to recheck due date, not send date; make configurable |
| 10-week timeline too tight if API work needed | Medium | High | Spike calendar API in Week 1; adjust scope (e.g., email-only at beta) if needed |

---

## Timeline & Milestones

| Week | Milestone |
|---|---|
| 1 | Calendar API audit complete; token security design approved |
| 2 | Data model confirmed; rebooking page wireframes signed off |
| 3–4 | Core flow built: URL generation, rebooking page, calendar write |
| 5 | Automated reminder cadence integrated; internal QA begins |
| 6 | Front-desk worklist built and tested |
| 7 | Security review; accessibility audit |
| 8 | Staging deploy; pilot clinic onboarding prep |
| 9 | Beta launch with 12 pilot clinics |
| 10 | Beta checkpoint: collect rebooking rate, call-time data, drop-off metrics |

---

## Next Steps

1. **Week 1 (P0):** Audit the existing Pawpath calendar API for write capability — this is the single largest technical risk and must be resolved before sprint planning.
2. **Week 1 (P0):** Confirm the data model supports "recheck due date" per patient visit; if not, scope a schema migration immediately.
3. **Before kickoff:** Calculate average revenue per recheck visit to quantify the business case and inform pilot clinic selection criteria.
4. **Week 1–2:** Define the signed-token expiry policy with the security and clinical ops teams.
5. **Week 2:** Finalize reminder cadence defaults (look-ahead window, send timing) with 2–3 pilot clinic managers before building.
6. **Week 9:** Establish a weekly data pull cadence from pilot clinics to track rebooking rate and call hours against targets in real time.

# Pawpath H2 Clinic Growth

Starting from 410 paying clinics and $1.9M ARR, Fernway Labs' Pawpath faces a compounding growth problem: a 2.1% monthly logo churn rate—concentrated in the first 90 days—erases new acquisitions almost as fast as they arrive (approximately 9 clinics lost per month, derived from the PM's figures). This OKR set addresses three interdependent levers: accelerating net clinic growth through multi-site expansion, eliminating early churn at its root, and converting onboarding from a specialist-dependent bottleneck into a scalable self-serve motion. **Critical timing flag: with today's date of October 15, 2026, only approximately 2.5 months of H2 remain. Targets below are set for December 31, 2026; however, the Gaps section recommends converting these immediately into a Q4 2026 + H1 2027 bridge cycle.**

---

## OKR Set

### Objective 1: Grow the Pawpath clinic base and revenue without increasing acquisition spend

*At 2.1% monthly churn, Pawpath needs to acquire more than 9 clinics per month just to stand still. Net growth requires reducing that drain and adding clinics via referral and multi-site channels—the only levers available without new paid budget.*

- **KR 1.1:** Increase paying clinics from 410 to **Target: 490** by December 31, 2026
- **KR 1.2:** Grow ARR from $1.9M to **Target: $2.35M** by December 31, 2026 *(assumes ARPU lift from multi-site contracts; this is a target, not a projection)*
- **KR 1.3:** Close **Target: 3** multi-site group contracts (≥ 5 clinic locations each) by December 31, 2026
- **KR 1.4:** Achieve **Target: 25%** of new clinic sign-ups sourced from existing-clinic referrals by December 31, 2026 *(baseline: to be established — see Gaps)*

---

### Objective 2: Eliminate first-90-day churn as the primary growth killer

*The 2.1% monthly churn rate is disproportionately concentrated in the first 90 days. Fixing early-lifecycle failure is the highest-leverage intervention available — it simultaneously improves net revenue retention and frees the onboarding team from reactive firefighting.*

- **KR 2.1:** Reduce monthly logo churn rate from 2.1% to **Target: 1.2%** by December 31, 2026
- **KR 2.2:** Increase 90-day retention for new clinic cohorts from **[baseline: to be measured — see Gaps]** to **Target: 80%** by December 31, 2026
- **KR 2.3:** Achieve median time-to-first-meaningful-use of **Target: ≤ 7 business days** for all clinics activated in Q4 2026 *(baseline: to be established — see Gaps)*
- **KR 2.4:** Deploy a churn-risk intervention playbook—built on the top **Target: 3** leading-indicator signals—and demonstrate that intervened at-risk clinics retain at a rate **Target: 15 percentage points** higher than unintervened controls by December 31, 2026

---

### Objective 3: Transform onboarding into a self-serve engine that unlocks multi-site sales capacity

*Three onboarding specialists currently carry the full activation load for every single-site clinic. Self-serve onboarding is the forcing function that frees those specialists to pursue high-value multi-site group deals — the only non-paid acquisition channel with meaningful ARR upside per contract.*

- **KR 3.1:** Reach **Target: 65%** of new single-site clinic activations completing onboarding end-to-end without specialist intervention by December 31, 2026
- **KR 3.2:** Confirm quality parity: self-serve clinic 90-day retention within **Target: 5 percentage points** of specialist-assisted clinic 90-day retention
- **KR 3.3:** Redirect **Target: ≥ 60%** of total onboarding specialist capacity toward multi-site group prospecting, deal support, and complex migrations by December 31, 2026 *(baseline hours per clinic: to be established — see Gaps)*
- **KR 3.4:** Reduce average onboarding-to-live calendar time from **[baseline: to be established]** to **Target: ≤ 10 business days** for self-serve clinics

---

## Expert Analysis, Gaps & Flags

### ⚠️ Sandbagging Check

| OKR | Verdict |
|---|---|
| KR 1.1 — 490 clinics | **Ambitious given ~2.5 months remaining.** Do not sandbag to 430–440; that merely offsets churn. If cycle resets to January, this is appropriately stretching. |
| KR 2.1 — 1.2% monthly churn | **Correct stretch level.** Cutting churn nearly in half signals genuine root-cause commitment. Sandbagging to 1.8% would make this unmeasurably different from doing nothing. |
| KR 3.1 — 65% self-serve activation | **Verify feasibility.** Requires the 9-engineer / 2-designer team to ship a materially improved in-app onboarding flow in ~2.5 months. De-risk by scoping an MVP, not a full redesign. |

### ⚠️ Missing Baselines (Blocks Execution)

| Missing Baseline | KR Affected | Action Owner |
|---|---|---|
| 90-day cohort retention rate | KR 2.2 | Analytics / Data |
| Referral-sourced sign-up % | KR 1.4 | Marketing / CRM |
| Onboarding-to-live calendar time | KR 3.4 | Onboarding Lead |
| Specialist hours per new clinic | KR 3.3 | Onboarding Lead |

**All four baselines must be established before October 29, 2026. Without them, KRs 2.2, 1.4, 3.3, and 3.4 are unmeasurable.**

### ⚠️ Timing Risk

Setting H2 OKRs on October 15, 2026 gives approximately 11 weeks of execution runway—too short for a standard 13-week OKR cycle. **Recommendation:** Treat this as a Q4 2026 sprint and lock the same objectives as H1 2027 OKRs immediately so the team has a full cycle to execute.

### ⚠️ KR Quality Notes

- **KR 2.4** originally risked being an output ("document signals"). It has been rewritten as an outcome: the intervention cohort must demonstrate a **Target: 15 percentage point** retention lift over controls. If the playbook is built but the lift is not measured, the KR is not complete.
- **KR 3.3** (specialist hour reallocation) is a proxy metric. Validate monthly by tracking multi-site pipeline value, not just time logs.

No company-level OKRs were provided. The following alignment assumptions **must be validated with Fernway Labs leadership before these OKRs are finalized:**

| Assumed Company Objective | Pawpath OKR Alignment |
|---|---|
| **Grow ARR** | O1 (clinic count + ARR), O2 (churn reduction = revenue retained) |
| **Improve unit economics** | O3 (self-serve lowers onboarding cost per clinic) |
| **Enter multi-site / enterprise segment** | O1 KR 1.3 + O3 KR 3.3 (capacity reallocation to group sales) |

# Why Clinics Switch to Pawpath
## Jobs-to-be-Done Analysis — Independent Vet Clinics

**Prepared for:** Pawpath Product Team | **Date:** 15 October 2026 | **Source:** 8 clinic-manager interviews (switches within the last year)

---

Based on eight interviews with clinic managers who switched to Pawpath within the last year, this analysis surfaces the functional, emotional, and social jobs driving adoption — and the specific failure moments that triggered the switch. The dominant prior stack (used by 6 of 8 respondents) was a paper diary combined with a shared spreadsheet, a combination that collapsed under three recurring pressures: unmanageable phone volume, scheduling errors that damaged client trust, and personal time lost to administrative overflow. The jobs below are direct derivatives of those pressures; figures are drawn exclusively from the PM's inputs, with any additions clearly labelled as assumptions or targets.

---

## Functional Jobs

These are the practical tasks clinic managers are trying to accomplish.

### Core Functional Jobs

- **When** the front desk is juggling walk-ins and calls simultaneously, **I want** a single source of truth for appointment slots, **so I can** book without checking two systems and creating gaps or overlaps.

- **When** a client calls to book outside staffed hours, **I want** the system to accept and confirm the appointment automatically, **so I can** stop fielding calls in the evening.

- **When** two staff members access the schedule at the same time, **I want** real-time conflict detection, **so I can** guarantee no two clients are assigned the same slot.

- **When** a no-show or cancellation happens, **I want** the freed slot surfaced immediately to waiting clients, **so I can** keep the day fully utilised without manual follow-up.

### Gap Identified

None of the eight interview quotes address **reminders and follow-up care scheduling** (e.g., annual vaccinations, post-op check-ins). This is a probable functional job that was not explored — and a missed onboarding hook. *Assumption to validate:* clinics currently manage recall reminders manually.

---

## Emotional Jobs

These are how clinic managers want to feel — or stop feeling.

- **When** I finish the clinical day, **I want** to know the next day's schedule is locked and confirmed, **so I can** switch off without anxiety that something was missed.

- **When** an error surfaces in front of a client, **I want** to feel competent and in control of my practice, **so I can** maintain confidence in the systems I run.

- **When** I am managing the clinic alone or understaffed, **I want** the software to absorb administrative load, **so I can** focus on patient care rather than coordination.

### Key Emotional Signal

*"I wanted my evenings back"* is the highest-stakes emotional job in the data set. It frames Pawpath not as scheduling software but as a **boundary-protection tool** — a reframe that should be prominent in acquisition messaging and the onboarding welcome sequence.

---

## Social Jobs

These are how clinic managers want to be perceived by others.

- **When** a client arrives and their appointment is not in the system, **I want** the booking to be unambiguously confirmed and visible, **so I can** be seen as a professional, organised practice — not one that loses records.

- **When** my team reviews the day's schedule, **I want** it to be accurate and unambiguous, **so I can** be trusted as the person responsible for clinic operations.

- **When** a client recommends the clinic to a friend, **I want** the booking experience to feel modern and frictionless, **so I can** reinforce a reputation that matches the quality of care we deliver.

### Key Social Signal

*"Double bookings embarrassed us in front of clients"* reveals that scheduling errors are **public failures**, not just operational ones. The social cost (lost trust, awkward confrontations) is likely as motivating as the operational cost. Onboarding copy and case studies should reference this explicitly.

---

## Hiring Criteria

What clinics evaluate — consciously or not — when choosing an appointment solution.

| Criterion | Signal from Interviews | Weight |
|---|---|---|
| **Eliminates double-booking** | Named directly in 8/8 interviews (implicit or explicit) | Critical |

# Pawpath North Star

Pawpath's business model — a flat monthly fee per clinic — lives or dies on renewal, and the PM's own data reveals the key: clinics that confirm at least 80% of appointments through Pawpath reminders renew at a significantly higher rate than those that do not. Today, only 52% of booked appointments are confirmed through the platform, meaning most clinics are operating below the threshold that predicts retention. ---

## North Star Metric

### **Appointment Confirmation Rate (ACR)**

> *The percentage of all booked appointments, across all active clinics, confirmed through Pawpath reminders in a rolling 30-day window.*

**Formula:** `(Appointments confirmed via Pawpath ÷ Total booked appointments) × 100`

**Current baseline:** 52%
**Renewal threshold (from PM input):** 80%
**Target:** 80% platform-wide *(Target: to be achieved within a timeline the team should now define — see Next Steps)*

### Why This Metric

ACR is the single number that unifies value for both customer segments:

- **For clinics:** A confirmed appointment means fewer no-shows, predictable chair time, and better revenue. The 80% threshold is not an arbitrary goal — it's the PM-validated boundary between clinics that churn and clinics that stay.
- **For pet owners:** Responding to a reminder and confirming an appointment is a low-friction act of care. It signals the product is working in the pet owner's life, not just sitting in a clinic's back office.
- **For Pawpath:** ACR is a leading indicator of renewal, the company's primary revenue event. Moving ACR up moves net revenue retention up.

### Expert Analysis: Why Not a Different Metric?

A common alternative would be **Daily Active Clinics** or **Reminders Sent**. Both fail as North Stars because they measure activity, not value. A clinic can send 1,000 reminders and achieve 20% confirmation — high activity, low value, high churn risk. ACR measures the *outcome* that matters, and that distinction is critical for a team deciding where to invest.

---

## Input Metrics

These are the four levers whose product directly controls ACR. Each has a clear owner and a clear direction.

### 1. Reminder Delivery Rate
**Definition:** % of booked appointments for which a Pawpath reminder was successfully delivered (not bounced, not blocked, not missing contact data).

**Why it matters:** A reminder that never arrives cannot be confirmed. If clinics have incomplete pet owner contact records, or if SMS/email deliverability is degraded, ACR has a ceiling that no engagement tactic can break through.

**Current baseline:** **TBD — this is Gap #1 to measure immediately.**

---

### 2. Reminder Engagement Rate
**Definition:** % of delivered reminders that receive at least one meaningful interaction (opened, link-clicked, or reply initiated) by the pet owner.

**Why it matters:** Delivery is necessary but not sufficient. If reminders land in spam, arrive at the wrong time of day, or carry unclear calls-to-action, pet owners won't act. This metric isolates the quality of the reminder itself — subject line, channel, timing, copy.

**Current baseline:** **TBD — Gap #2.**

---

### 3. Confirmation Completion Rate
**Definition:** % of engaged pet owners who complete the confirmation action (tap "Confirm," reply "YES," or equivalent) within the reminder flow.

**Why it matters:** This is the conversion step — the moment value is actually created. Friction here (too many steps, broken links, unclear instructions) directly suppresses ACR even when delivery and engagement are healthy. This is the highest-leverage UX surface in the product.

**Current baseline:** **TBD — Gap #3.**

---

### 4. Clinic Appointment Coverage Rate
**Definition:** % of a clinic's appointment types and booking sources that are actively routed through Pawpath's reminder workflow.

**Why it matters:** Many SaaS tools suffer "partial adoption" — a clinic may use Pawpath for online bookings but not for phone-in appointments, or for wellness visits but not for surgical follow-ups. If 40% of a clinic's appointments never enter the Pawpath pipeline, ACR for that clinic is capped at 60% regardless of how well the reminder flow performs. |---|---|
| **Pet Owner Opt-out Rate** | Rising opt-outs signal reminder fatigue. Increasing reminder frequency to boost ACR can cannibalize future confirmations. *Target: hold opt-out rate flat or declining as ACR rises.* |

# Positioning Pawpath

Pawpath sits in a gap that most scheduling tools ignore: independent vet clinics are not salons, and they are not hospital systems. They need software that understands species, treatment follow-up, and the reality that a solo practice manager cannot spend a week on implementation. The three attributes Pawpath already owns—species-aware scheduling, treatment-tied recheck reminders, and a one-afternoon setup—add up to a defensible position in a market category that almost no direct competitor has named first. This document works through April Dunford's five-step framework, surfaces the gaps in the current inputs, and closes with concrete actions the PM should take next.

---

## Step 1 — Competitive Alternatives

What do target clinics actually do today when they don't have Pawpath?

- **Paper diaries and wall planners** — Zero software cost, no learning curve, but zero automation. Recheck reminders live in someone's head or a sticky note.
- **Generic online booking tools built for salons or beauty** (e.g., Booksy-style tools) — Appointment types are flat; no concept of species, no clinical context, reminder logic is date-only.
- **The scheduling module inside a large practice-management suite** — Clinically aware but designed for multi-site hospital groups. High cost, long implementation, functionality that overwhelms a 3-vet practice.

**Gap the PM should fill:** Confirm which alternative is most common in the current customer base. That dominant alternative defines the contrast story in all sales and marketing copy. If most customers came from paper diaries, the hero message is different than if they came from a large PMS.

---

## Step 2 — Unique Attributes

What does Pawpath have or do that none of the alternatives can easily replicate?

| Attribute | Why it's hard to copy |
|---|---|
| **Species-aware visit lengths** | Requires a veterinary-specific data model; salon tools use flat appointment types; PMS suites have it but hide it behind complexity |
| **Recheck reminders tied to the treatment given** | Requires linking the scheduling layer to a clinical concept (treatment); no generic booking tool has this; PMS suites have recall modules but they're separate, costly add-ons |
| **One-afternoon setup** | A deliberate architectural choice; large PMS suites cannot match this without dismantling their onboarding model |
| **Retention signal: "reminders are the reason they stay"** | This is a revealed preference data point—customers are telling you the highest-value feature unprompted |

**Expert observation:** The retention signal is your most important business input and it is currently underused. It tells you that the recheck reminder is not a nice-to-have—it is the core product value. Everything else (species-aware scheduling, fast setup) reduces friction to getting customers to the point where they experience the reminder.

---

## Step 3 — Value Those Attributes Enable

Translate attributes into outcomes the clinic owner and practice manager actually care about.

### Species-aware visit lengths →
- **Fewer scheduling gaps and overruns.** A rabbit dental and a dog vaccine are not the same appointment. Getting the block length right reduces the chaos that frustrates both staff and pet owners.
- **Lower cognitive load on the front desk.** Staff stop manually padding time or arguing about appointment length.

### Treatment-tied recheck reminders →
- **Higher recheck compliance without manual chasing.** Rechecks that happen generate additional visit revenue and demonstrate clinical quality. Rechecks that don't happen create liability exposure and revenue leakage.
- **Better patient outcomes.** This is the clinical story that resonates with vets who went to school to practice medicine, not to manage a calendar.
- **Differentiated client experience.** Pet owners receive a reminder that references their specific treatment ("Time for Bella's post-op recheck"), not a generic "your appointment is due" message.

### One-afternoon setup →
- **Zero disruption to a practice that cannot close for an implementation project.** A 3-vet clinic has no IT department and no tolerance for a week of downtime.
- **Low switching risk.** The setup cost is so low that the fear of being wrong evaporates.

**Gap:** The PM has no quantified outcome data yet. Target metrics to gather from existing customers:
- **Target to validate:** Average increase in recheck visit rate after adopting Pawpath (expressed as %, to be measured)
- **Target to validate:** Reduction in no-shows or manual reminder calls (hours per week saved, to be measured)
- These are not figures available yet—treat them as **assumptions to validate** in the next customer interview cycle.

---

## Step 4 — Target Customers Who Care Most

Not every vet clinic is the right fit. Narrow to the segment that feels the pain hardest.

### Best-fit profile (ICP)
- **Independent clinic, 2–8 vets** (as stated by PM)
- **Current state:** Using paper diaries or a salon booking tool — they lack clinical scheduling entirely, so the delta between their today and Pawpath is enormous
- **Practice type:** Mixed-species or exotic-heavy practices will feel species-aware scheduling most acutely; high-recheck-volume practices (oncology, dentistry, post-surgery) will retain on reminders fastest
- **Decision-maker:** Practice owner or practice manager, not a hospital administrator — they move faster and control the budget directly
- **Attitude:** Frustrated with workarounds; not resistant to software, but burned by complexity before

### Segment to deprioritize (for now)
- Clinics inside a corporate group — they have a mandated PMS and no authority to add tools
- Single-vet practices — setup ROI is real but the network effect of scheduling complexity is lower; they may churn faster

**Gap:** The PM has not specified how many paying customers Pawpath has today, what industries or geographies are represented, or whether the 2–8 vet band was derived from data or intuition. **Assumption to validate:** The 2–8 vet definition is directionally correct but should be tested against actual customer data (e.g., do current customers cluster there, or do some 10-vet practices buy?).

---

## Step 5 — Market Category

The category you declare determines what competitors you are compared to, what buyers expect to pay, and what questions they ask in a demo.

### Category recommendation: **Veterinary Recheck & Scheduling Software**

**Why not "practice management"?** That category is owned by large suites. Entering it positions Pawpath as the cheap, limited alternative to Cornerstone or AVImark.

**Why not "appointment scheduling"?** That is the salon-tool category. It commoditises Pawpath and makes price the differentiator.

**Why "Veterinary Recheck & Scheduling"?** It does three things:

# Reminder Send-Time Test

Pawpath currently sends recheck reminders 3 days before the due date, achieving a 69% rebooking rate. This experiment tests whether shifting the send time to 7 days before the due date increases rebooking by giving pet owners more planning runway. With ~24,000 reminders sent monthly across 410 clinics, the test can reach statistical significance in approximately 6 weeks at a 50/50 traffic split—assuming a minimum detectable effect (MDE) of 2 percentage points (an assumption; see below). The design randomizes at the **pet-owner level**, stratified by clinic, to maximize power while preventing within-owner contamination. Two critical gaps require PM resolution before launch: whether a follow-up reminder is sent for non-converters in the 7-day arm, and how "rebooking" is operationally defined.

---

## Hypothesis

**If** recheck reminders are sent 7 days before the due date instead of 3 days, **then** the rebooking rate will increase **because** pet owners have more scheduling flexibility earlier in the week and face fewer last-minute conflicts that block action.

---

## Primary Metric

**Rebooking rate** — the proportion of reminder recipients who complete a confirmed booking within 14 days of reminder delivery.

- **Operationalization gap (PM action required):** Confirm whether "rebooking" means: (a) booking created, (b) booking confirmed by clinic, or (c) appointment attended. Attendance rate is the most meaningful but requires a longer attribution window.
- **Attribution window:** 14 days post-send for Control (3-day arm); 18 days post-send for Treatment (7-day arm), so both windows close on the same calendar date relative to the due date.

---

## Guardrail Metrics

These metrics must not degrade significantly; a breach pauses or kills the experiment.

| Guardrail | Direction | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| **Appointment show-up rate** | Must not decrease | A higher booking rate is worthless if no-shows spike |
| **Reminder unsubscribe rate** | Must not increase | Earlier reminders may feel intrusive |
| **Same-day/last-minute cancellation rate** | Must not increase | 7-day bookings may be more likely to cancel before the appointment |
| **Inbound support contacts per reminder sent** | Must not increase | Signals owner confusion about the earlier timing |
| **Revenue per reminder sent** | Monitor only | Downstream signal; not a stopping criterion alone |

---

## Minimum Detectable Effect

- **Assumption:** A lift of **2 percentage points** (69% → 71%) is the smallest effect that justifies permanently shifting send-time infrastructure and potential downstream scheduling load for 410 clinics.
- **PM action required:** Validate this threshold with the business team. A smaller MDE (e.g., 1pp) would require ~4× more reminders and is likely impractical given volume.

---

## Sample Size Calculation

**Inputs:**
- Baseline rebooking rate (p₁): **69%** (provided)
- Target rebooking rate (p₂): **71%** (Assumption: 2pp MDE)
- Significance level (α): **0.05**, two-tailed
- Statistical power (1−β): **0.80**
- z-scores: z₀.₀₂₅ = 1.96, z₀.₂₀ = 0.84
- Traffic split: 50/50

**Calculation:**

```
n = (z_α/2 + z_β)² × 2 × p̄(1−p̄) / (p₂−p₁)²
p̄ = (0.69 + 0.71) / 2 = 0.70

n = (1.96 + 0.84)² × 2 × 0.70 × 0.30 / (0.02)²
n = 7.84 × 0.42 / 0.0004
n ≈ 8,232 per arm
Total ≈ 16,500 reminders
```

**Note on clinic-level randomization (rejected):** Randomizing by clinic would require ~545 clinics per arm (after applying a design effect of ~3.9 for clustering), far exceeding the available 410 clinics. **Pet-owner randomization is required** to achieve adequate power.

---

## Expected Duration

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| Monthly reminder volume | 24,000 (provided) |
| Reminders per arm per month (50/50 split) | 12,000 |
| Reminders needed per arm | ~8,200 |
| Minimum calendar time to reach n | ~3 weeks |
| **Recommended run duration** | **6 weeks** |

**Why 6 weeks, not 3?** A 3-week window risks catching a single seasonal pattern (e.g., a holiday weekend or school break). Six weeks spans at least one full monthly billing/scheduling cycle for most clinics and reduces week-of-week noise from clinic-size variation.

---

## Randomization Unit

**Unit: Pet owner** (all pets belonging to the same owner receive the same treatment arm)

- **Stratification:** Randomize within clinic-size strata (e.g., small: <30 reminders/month; medium: 30–80; large: >80) to prevent imbalance caused by the high variance in clinic size across the 410 clinics.
- **Assignment persistence:** An owner's arm assignment is locked for the full 6-week experiment. If they receive multiple reminders during the window, each reminder follows the same timing arm.
- **Exclusion criteria (PM to confirm):** New owners with no prior reminder history; owners who have opted out of reminders; reminders for appointments booked same-day or next-day (ineligible for 7-day treatment).

---

## Analysis Plan

### Primary Analysis
- **Test:** Two-proportion z-test on rebooking rate, comparing Control vs. Treatment
- **Estimand:** Intention-to-treat (ITT) — all owners assigned to each arm, regardless of whether the reminder was opened
- **Significance threshold:** p < 0.05 (two-tailed); report 95% confidence interval on the absolute rate difference

### Secondary Analyses
- **Heterogeneous treatment effects (HTE):** Segment results by clinic size stratum, species (dog vs. cat if available), and reminder channel (email vs. SMS if applicable) to detect differential effects that the primary metric may mask
- **Survival analysis:** Time-to-booking curve by arm, to understand whether the 7-day arm books earlier in relative time and whether that translates to fewer last-minute appointments
- **Guardrail checks:** Run one-sided tests (α = 0.10) on each guardrail metric to flag degradation

### Correction for Multiple Testing
- Apply Bonferroni correction across the 5 guardrail metrics (adjusted α = 0.01 per guardrail) to control family-wise error rate

---

## Potential Pitfalls

### 🚩 Novelty Effect
- **Risk level: Low–Medium.** Reminders are a passive channel (owners don't know they're in an experiment), so novelty-driven behavior change is less likely than in UI tests. However, the first reminder an owner receives in the experiment may prompt unusually high engagement simply because the timing feels different.
- **Mitigation:** Exclude the first 3 days of data ("burn-in") from the primary analysis and verify that week-1 vs. week-6 booking rates are stable within each arm.

### 🚩 Simpson's Paradox
- **Risk level: High.** Clinic size varies "a lot" (PM's words). If large clinics are over-represented in one arm by chance, aggregate rebooking rates will be distorted—large clinics may have systematically higher or lower baseline rates.
- **Mitigation:** Stratified randomization by clinic size (see Randomization Unit) prevents this at assignment. Additionally, run a covariate-adjusted analysis (ANCOVA with clinic size and baseline clinic rebooking rate as covariates) as the primary estimator, not just the raw rate difference.

### 🚩 Interference Between Arms (SUTVA Violation)
- **Risk:** A pet owner assigned to the 7-day arm might discuss their reminder timing with a neighbor also enrolled in the 3-day arm (unlikely but possible in tight communities).
- **Mitigation:** Low priority; standard reminder experiments accept this risk. No action needed unless results are anomalous.

### 🚩 Follow-Up Reminder Gap
- **Critical gap (PM must resolve):** Does the 7-day arm also receive a 3-day reminder if they haven't booked yet? If yes, the experiment is testing "7-day + 3-day" vs. "3-day alone"—a different question. If no, non-converters in the 7-day arm lose a touchpoint, which could suppress rebooking rates and confound results. **Document the exact reminder sequence for each arm before launch.**

### 🚩 Seasonal Confound
- **Risk:** A 6-week window starting in, say, late November will overlap with holiday scheduling disruptions that disproportionately affect early-booked (7-day) appointments.
- **Mitigation:** Avoid launching during major holiday periods. Target: **Assumption: launch in a neutral 6-week window** (e.g., early February–mid March or early September–mid October).

---

## Expert Analysis & Gaps

Beyond what the PM provided, the following warrant investigation before or alongside this experiment:

1. **Appointment completion rate is the true north star.** Booking rate is a leading indicator; if 7-day bookings cancel at higher rates, the intervention could net-negative despite a higher primary metric. Add show-up rate as a guardrail immediately.
2. **The 69% baseline hides clinic-level variance.** Before running the experiment, pull the distribution of rebooking rates across all 410 clinics. If variance is high (e.g., some clinics at 45%, others at 90%), the experiment's power estimate may be optimistic and segment-level HTE analysis becomes essential.
3. **No data on why 31% don't rebook.** Support's hypothesis is plausible but unvalidated. A brief survey or support-ticket analysis of non-converters would strengthen the causal story and reveal whether timing is the actual barrier (vs. cost, convenience, or pet health concerns).
4. **SMS vs. email channel split unknown.** If channels have different baseline rates, unequal channel distribution across arms could confound results. Confirm channel is balanced or block-randomize by channel.

---

## Next Steps

1. **[Immediate — PM]** Resolve the follow-up reminder question: does the 7-day arm receive a 3-day reminder for non-converters? This changes the experiment design fundamentally.
2. **[Immediate — PM]** Align on the operational definition of "rebooking" (created vs. confirmed vs. attended) with the data/engineering team.
3. **[This week — Data]** Pull clinic-level rebooking rate distribution to validate the 69% baseline and check variance; reassess MDE if variance is high.
4. **[This week — Engineering]** Confirm pet-owner-level assignment is technically feasible in the reminder system; verify stratified randomization by clinic size can be implemented.
5. **[Before launch — PM]** Select a launch window that avoids major holidays; target Assumption: a neutral 6-week period.
6. **[Before launch — Analytics]** Pre-register the analysis plan (primary metric, guardrail thresholds, HTE segments) to prevent post-hoc p-hacking.
7. **[Post-experiment]** If the 7-day arm wins on rebooking but show-up rates drop, design a follow-on test combining 7-day + 3-day reminders vs. 3-day alone.

# Pawpath Waitlist — User Stories

Pawpath's current paper-based waitlist forces front-desk staff to make manual calls when appointment slots cancel, creating delays and missed fill opportunities. This document defines eight INVEST-compliant user stories — grouped across four epics — for an automated SMS-driven waitlist that detects freed slots, matches them to the first eligible pet owner, and holds each slot for **15 minutes** pending confirmation. Expert analysis identifies six critical assumption gaps the team must resolve before sprint planning, including the precise definition of "matching," the owner opt-in channel, and cascade-depth limits.

---

## Assumptions & Identified Gaps

| # | Gap | Assumption Used | Action Required |
|---|-----|----------------|-----------------|
| 1 | How "matching" is defined | Appointment type + pet species + clinic location | PM to confirm criteria |
| 2 | Owner opt-in channel | Web link or in-clinic QR code | PM to confirm enrollment UX |
| 3 | Cascade logic after no response | Offer moves to next owner; Target: max 5 cascades per slot | Confirm rule with PM + engineering |
| 4 | SMS reply keywords | Owners reply **YES** to accept, **NO** to decline, **STOP** to opt out | Confirm with SMS provider |
| 5 | Concurrent entries | One active waitlist entry per pet per clinic at a time | Confirm business rule |
| 6 | Operating hours scope | Per-clinic hours configured in admin settings | Confirm with front-desk workflow |

---

## Epic 1: Waitlist Enrollment

**Goal:** Enable pet owners to join the digital waitlist and define their availability so offers are relevant and actionable.

### Story 1.1 — Join the Waitlist

**As a** pet owner, **I want to** add myself to the clinic's digital waitlist, **so that** I am automatically notified when a suitable appointment opens up.

```gherkin
Given I am a registered Pawpath user with at least one pet profile
When I complete waitlist enrollment by selecting appointment type, pet, and clinic
Then my entry is saved with an enrollment timestamp and I receive an SMS confirming I am on the waitlist

Given I attempt to enroll for the same pet, appointment type, and clinic a second time
When I submit the duplicate enrollment
Then the system rejects it and returns the message: "You are already on the waitlist for this slot type"
```

### Story 1.2 — Set Availability Preferences

**As a** pet owner, **I want to** specify the days and time windows when I am available, **so that** I only receive slot offers I can realistically accept.

```gherkin
Given I am enrolled on the waitlist
When I set my availability to weekdays between 9 am and 1 pm
Then the system only sends me offers for slots that fall within that window

Given a freed slot falls outside my specified availability window
When the system runs matching logic
Then my entry is skipped and the offer passes to the next eligible owner without notifying me
```

---

## Epic 2: Slot Detection & Matching

**Goal:** Automatically identify freed slots and select the correct owner from the waitlist without manual staff intervention.

### Story 2.1 — Automatic Slot Detection

**As a** front-desk staff member, **I want** the system to detect a cancelled appointment automatically, **so that** I do not need to manually trigger the waitlist process.

```gherkin
Given an appointment is marked "Cancelled" in the scheduling system
When the cancellation is saved
Then the system immediately flags the freed slot and initiates waitlist matching — no manual action required

Given the freed slot falls outside the clinic's configured operating hours
When the cancellation is saved
Then the system queues the slot for matching at the start of the next operating day and posts a dashboard alert for staff
```

### Story 2.2 — First-Match Owner Selection

**As a** pet owner on the waitlist, **I want** the system to select me based on my queue position and matching criteria, **so that** the process is fair and relevant to my pet's needs.

```gherkin
Given multiple owners are waitlisted for the same appointment type at the same clinic
When a matching slot is freed
Then the system selects the owner with the earliest enrollment timestamp who satisfies all matching criteria: appointment type, pet species, clinic, and availability window

Given the top-ranked owner already has an unanswered offer in progress
When the system runs matching for a newly freed slot
Then that owner is skipped and the next eligible owner is selected
```

---

## Epic 3: SMS Offer & Hold Window

**Goal:** Deliver a timely, actionable SMS offer and enforce the 15-minute hold window with clean cascade logic.

### Story 3.1 — Receive a Slot Offer via SMS

**As a** pet owner, **I want to** receive an SMS when a matching slot becomes available, **so that** I can claim it instantly without calling the clinic.

```gherkin
Given I am the top-ranked matching owner
When a slot is freed and I am selected by the system
Then I receive an SMS within 60 seconds (Target) containing: clinic name, appointment type, date, time, and "Reply YES to book or NO to decline — offer expires in 15 minutes"

Given I receive the offer SMS
When I reply YES within the 15-minute window
Then the appointment is confirmed in my name, the slot is removed from the freed pool, and I receive a booking confirmation SMS with full appointment details
```

### Story 3.2 — Handle Expired or Declined Offers

**As a** pet owner, **I want** the system to cascade the offer to the next person if I decline or do not respond, **so that** the slot fills efficiently and I stay on the waitlist for future openings.

```gherkin
Given I received a slot offer SMS
When I reply NO
Then I receive a confirmation that I have declined, I remain on the waitlist, and the offer is immediately sent to the next matching owner

Given I received a slot offer SMS
When 15 minutes elapse without any reply
Then the hold expires, the slot cascades to the next matching owner, and I receive an SMS notifying me the offer has lapsed but I remain on the waitlist
```

---

## Epic 4: Staff Operations & Visibility

**Goal:** Give front-desk staff real-time control and give clinic managers the data to evaluate system performance.

### Story 4.1 — Manage the Waitlist Dashboard

**As a** front-desk staff member, **I want to** view the live waitlist and manually reorder or remove entries, **so that** I can handle edge cases the automation cannot resolve.

```gherkin
Given I am logged in as front-desk staff
When I open the Waitlist Dashboard
Then I see all active entries sorted by enrollment timestamp, each showing: owner name, pet name, appointment type, and availability window

Given an owner calls in to withdraw from the waitlist
When I select their entry and confirm removal
Then their entry is deleted and they receive an SMS confirming they have been removed
```

### Story 4.2 — Monitor Waitlist Fill Rate

**As a** clinic manager, **I want to** see a summary of how cancelled slots were resolved, **so that** I can evaluate system effectiveness and adjust staffing decisions.

```gherkin
Given I am logged in as a clinic manager
When I open Waitlist Reports and select a date range
Then I see: total freed slots, slots filled via SMS waitlist, slots filled manually, and slots that went unfilled — each shown as a count and percentage

Given my configured fill-rate alert threshold is reached (Assumption: configurable; Target: alert at below 70% for a rolling 30-day period)
When the system recalculates weekly
Then I receive an email alert prompting me to review waitlist depth or matching criteria
```

---

## Expert Recommendations

- **Define "matching" in Sprint 0.** Without a precise algorithm, Story 2.2 cannot be reliably estimated or built. This is the single highest-risk dependency.
- **Add an SMS opt-out story to the backlog now.** Owners must be able to reply STOP to unsubscribe (Assumption: regulatory requirement in target market). Omitting this risks compliance issues at launch.
- **Set a cascade depth limit.** Uncontrolled cascading could generate excessive SMS volume. Confirm the Target: 5-cascade cap with PM before Epic 3 is built.
- **Plan a secondary notification channel.** SMS delivery can fail silently. Scope a fallback (email or in-app push, if a Pawpath app exists) as a follow-on story after core flow is stable.
- **Address data retention.** Waitlist timestamps and SMS logs are personal data. Confirm retention policy with legal before the data model is finalised.

---

## Next Steps

1. **Validate all six assumption gaps** (see table) in a PM + engineering + front-desk discovery session — schedule before the next sprint planning ceremony.
2. **Document the match algorithm** (appointment type, pet species, clinic, availability window) as a shared definition in the team wiki so Story 2.2 can be estimated accurately.
3. **Select and contract an SMS provider** and verify two-way keyword handling (YES / NO / STOP) to unblock all of Epic 3.
4. **Add an opt-out (STOP) user story** to the backlog immediately to ensure compliance is built in from day one, not retrofitted.
5. **Prioritise epics for Sprint 1:** Recommend starting with Epic 2 (slot detection) and Epic 3 (SMS offer) as the highest-value, highest-risk items; defer Epic 4 reporting to a later sprint.
6. **Test SMS copy with Target: 3–5 real pet owners** before build begins to confirm the offer message is clear and the YES/NO mechanic is intuitive.

# Pawpath SWOT

## Executive Summary

Pawpath enters H2 with a defensible foothold — 410 independent vet clinics, $1.9M ARR, and a reminder feature that clinics demonstrably value — but faces a narrowing window before free scheduling bundles from two large practice-management suites erode its positioning in the market. The core strategic question for H2 is not whether to defend or grow, but **where to widen the moat before commoditization accelerates**. This analysis finds that lab system integrations represent the highest-leverage investment: they solve a real clinic pain point, create data stickiness that free bundlers cannot easily replicate, and open a credible upsell motion on a base that already trusts Pawpath. A team of 14 cannot fight on every front, so the recommendations below are deliberately focused on sequenced, high-return bets rather than platform sprawl.

---

## Strengths

- **Proven reminder feature** — already differentiated enough that 410 clinics pay for it; this is validated product-market fit in at least one workflow.
- **410 independent clinic relationships** — a warm, paying distribution network and a direct feedback loop that large suites lack at this segment.
- **$1.9M ARR** — sufficient recurring revenue to fund a focused H2 roadmap without distress-driven decisions.
- **Small, lean team of 14** — can move faster than enterprise software vendors and pivot without committee approval.

---

## Weaknesses

- **No lab system integrations** — a significant workflow gap; clinics run diagnostics constantly, and fragmented tooling creates friction that a competitor could exploit.
- **Narrow value proposition** — currently anchored to reminders/scheduling; limited surface area means limited reasons to stay if a competitor matches that feature.
- **Team of 14 caps execution bandwidth** — every new initiative competes for the same small pool of engineering and support capacity.
- **Concentration in independent clinics** — this segment is price-sensitive and fragmented, making upsell harder and churn risk higher than in consolidated chains. *(Assumption to validate: churn rate and average contract value.)*

---

## Opportunities

- **Lab integration gap** — no known current offering bridges appointment workflows with in-clinic lab results for independent practices; first-mover here creates switching cost.
- **Independent clinic identity** — large suites are designed for multi-location chains; independent owners want tools built for them, not adapted for them.
- **Workflow expansion** — reminders are one touch point; client communication, post-visit follow-up, and inventory alerts are adjacent workflows Pawpath could own.
- **Partner-led integrations** — lab hardware vendors (Target: identify 2–3 in H2) may have API programs that reduce Pawpath's engineering lift for integrations.
- **ARR growth via upsell** — 410 existing clinics are an untapped upsell pool; even a modest increase in ARPU (Target: validate current ARPU baseline) materially moves ARR without new logo acquisition.

---

## Threats

- **Two large suites bundling free scheduling** — direct pressure on Pawpath's core use case; "good enough for free" is a powerful message to cost-conscious independent owners.
- **Feature commoditization** — as scheduling becomes table stakes, Pawpath's primary differentiation erodes unless it moves up the value chain.
- **Talent and execution risk** — a team of 14 building integrations while maintaining the core product and supporting 410 clients is genuinely stretched. A key engineer departure is a material risk.
- **Consolidation in the independent clinic segment** — if corporate vet groups acquire independent clinics, the addressable base may shrink and buying decisions shift to procurement teams favoring incumbent suites.

---

## Strategic Action Mapping

### SO Strategies — Use Strengths to Capture Opportunities

- **Convert reminder trust into integration adoption:** Use the goodwill earned with 410 clinics to beta-test lab integrations with a subset of high-engagement practices. The existing relationship lowers adoption friction significantly.
- **Position $1.9M ARR as a platform signal:** Reinvest a defined portion of ARR (Target: establish H2 R&D budget allocation) into integration infrastructure — labs today, inventory or telehealth tomorrow — establishing Pawpath as the independent clinic operating layer, not a scheduling point tool.
- **Leverage clinic density for partnership negotiation:** 410 paying clinics is a credible number to bring to a lab vendor partnership conversation; use it to negotiate API access or co-marketing rather than building integrations from scratch.

### WO Strategies — Overcome Weaknesses via Opportunities

- **Build integrations through partnerships, not only internal engineering:** Given a team of 14, Pawpath cannot custom-build every integration. Identify lab vendors with existing API programs to close the lab gap without burning the team. *(Assumption to validate: which lab vendors have developer programs.)*
- **Use the lab integration to justify a price tier:** Today's narrow feature set constrains pricing power. A lab-connected tier creates a defensible reason to charge more, addressing both the narrow value proposition weakness and the upsell opportunity simultaneously.
- **Fund a dedicated integration hire in H2:** One integration-focused engineer or technical partnerships manager materially expands execution capacity without doubling headcount. This is the leverage point that unlocks the other WO strategies.

### ST Strategies — Use Strengths to Counter Threats

- **Out-specialize the bundlers on independent clinic workflow:** Large suites bundle scheduling as a checkbox; Pawpath should make its reminder and communication layer so deeply tailored to independent vet workflows (SOAP note follow-ups, vaccination cadences, species-specific reminders) that "free but generic" is a visible downgrade.
- **Accelerate switching costs before bundling takes hold:** Use the 410-clinic base to roll out features — lab integration, two-way client messaging, outcome tracking — that embed Pawpath into daily clinical operations. The deeper the integration, the higher the switching cost, regardless of what competitors bundle.
- **Establish an independent clinic community:** A Pawpath user community (slack group, quarterly webinars, peer benchmarking) turns customers into advocates and creates a retention moat that is structurally invisible to large suite competitors focused on enterprise accounts.

### WT Strategies — Minimize Weaknesses and Avoid Threats

- **Explicitly deprioritize basic scheduling feature development in H2:** Do not compete with free. Redirect any engineering capacity that would go to parity scheduling features toward differentiated workflow depth instead.
- **Build a documented succession plan for critical roles:** With a team of 14, one or two key departures can stall roadmap delivery. A lightweight knowledge-sharing and cross-training protocol reduces execution fragility without significant cost.
- **Define a customer retention playbook for at-risk clinics:** Proactively identify the clinics most likely to churn to a free bundle (e.g., low feature usage, single-user accounts) and intervene with value demonstrations or account reviews before they evaluate alternatives.

---

## Top 3 Prioritized Strategic Actions

1. **Launch a lab integration beta with a subset of existing clinics by end of H2** *(Target: 20–30 clinics as beta cohort — validate target with team capacity).* This is the single highest-leverage move: it differentiates Pawpath from free bundlers, increases ARPU, and deepens switching costs simultaneously. Pursue via partner API first to conserve engineering bandwidth.

2. **Deepen the reminder/communication layer to be species- and workflow-specific, not generic.** This is the fastest path to making the core product un-substitutable. It requires minimal new infrastructure, is achievable with the existing team of 14, and directly counters the "good enough for free" threat by making Pawpath's version visibly superior for independent vet workflows.

3. **Add one integration-focused role (engineer or technical partnerships) in H2.** The team of 14 is the binding constraint on every other strategic action. A targeted hire that unlocks integration execution capacity is a force multiplier, not just a headcount addition. Prioritize this before scoping any new product workstream.

---

## Next Steps

1. **Validate ARPU and churn rate** — current ARR and clinic count are known; ARPU and churn are the missing inputs needed to size upsell opportunity and assess retention risk. Pull this data before finalizing H2 budget allocation.
2. **Map lab vendor API landscape** — assign one team member to identify which lab hardware or diagnostic vendors serving independent vet clinics have existing developer/partner programs. Complete within 3 weeks.
3. **Define H2 R&D budget split** — with this SWOT as input, hold a focused session to allocate H2 engineering capacity across: (a) lab integration, (b) reminder depth, and (c) retention tooling. Set explicit capacity limits to prevent scope creep.
4. **Draft job description for integration-focused hire** — start the pipeline now; hiring cycles are long relative to an H2 window.
5. **Identify 20–30 beta clinic candidates for lab integration** — pull from the 410-clinic base based on engagement signals and champion relationships to ensure a high-quality feedback loop.

# Pawpath Market Size

Pawpath targets independent veterinary clinics (2–8 vets) in a single country, priced at $390 per clinic per month. Based on Fernway's CRM count of 6,200 qualifying clinics, the **Total Addressable Market is ~$29.0M ARR**. Restricting to the 70% of clinics that lack a dedicated scheduling tool (per the PM's estimate) yields a **Serviceable Addressable Market of ~$20.3M ARR**. Under the assumption (clearly labeled below) that Pawpath captures 10% of that unserved segment by end of Year 3, the **Serviceable Obtainable Market is ~$2.0M ARR** — a credible first-revenue milestone for a single-country SaaS product. Both top-down and bottom-up approaches converge on the same figures because the CRM-sourced clinic count is the binding constraint in both models; the key validation gap is sales-capacity data, which the PM should supply before finalizing board projections.

---

## Market Definition

- **Customer:** Independent veterinary clinics operating 2–8 vets in Fernway's home country
- **Product:** Pawpath scheduling SaaS
- **Price:** $390 per clinic per month ($4,680 per clinic per year)
- **Geography:** One country (no cross-border expansion modeled here)
- **Exclusions:** Corporate chains, solo-vet practices, multi-location enterprises — all outside the 2–8 vet bracket

---

## TAM — Total Addressable Market

> *The maximum annual revenue if every qualifying clinic in the country subscribed.*

### Top-Down

Starting from the total known universe:

- **Total qualifying clinics (source: Fernway CRM):** 6,200
- Revenue per clinic per year: $390 × 12 = **$4,680**
- **TAM = 6,200 × $4,680 = $29,016,000 ≈ $29.0M ARR**

### Bottom-Up

Building from unit economics:

- Unit: one clinic subscription
- Annual contract value (ACV): **$4,680**
- Addressable customer count (CRM): **6,200**
- **TAM = 6,200 × $4,680 = $29.0M ARR**

**Note:** Both approaches yield identical figures because the CRM count is the only available market-sizing anchor. This is a known gap — see Gaps & Risks.

---

## SAM — Serviceable Addressable Market

> *Revenue accessible today, filtered to clinics with a real near-term pain point.*

### Top-Down

Applying the "no dedicated scheduling tool" filter the PM provided:

- Clinics without a dedicated scheduling tool: 6,200 × 70% = **4,340 clinics**
- **SAM = 4,340 × $4,680 = $20,311,200 ≈ $20.3M ARR**

### Bottom-Up

- Addressable buyer: clinic administrator or lead vet at one of the 4,340 unserved clinics
- Annual spend unlocked per customer: **$4,680**
- **SAM = 4,340 × $4,680 = $20.3M ARR**

**Key assumption to validate:** The 70% "unserved" figure comes from a PM estimate, not a formal survey. If the true figure is 50%, SAM drops to ~$14.5M ARR; if 80%, it rises to ~$23.2M ARR. The PM should validate this with a sample outreach or a short sales-team audit before presenting to the board.

---

## SOM — Serviceable Obtainable Market

> *Revenue realistically capturable within a defined planning horizon.*

### Assumptions

| # | Assumption | Value | Label |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | SAM capture rate by end of Year 3 | 10% of SAM | **Target** |
| 2 | Target clinics signed by end of Year 3 | 434 clinics | **Target** (derived) |
| 3 | Churn rate | TBD — no figure provided | **Assumption to validate** |
| 4 | Sales cycle length | TBD | **Assumption to validate** |
| 5 | Sales headcount required to reach 434 clinics | TBD | **Assumption to validate** |

### Calculation

- **Target clinics:** 4,340 × 10% = **434 clinics**
- Monthly run rate at target: 434 × $390 = **$169,260 MRR**
- **SOM = 434 × $4,680 = $2,031,120 ≈ $2.0M ARR** *(based on 10% capture target — not a data-backed result)*

**Sensitivity:**

| Capture rate | Clinics | ARR |
|---|---|---|
| 5% (conservative) | 217 | ~$1.0M |
| **10% (target)** | **434** | **~$2.0M** |
| 15% (optimistic) | 651 | ~$3.0M |

---

## Growth Drivers

- **Unserved base is large:** 4,340 clinics running on manual or general-purpose tools represent genuine switching opportunity — no incumbent-displacement needed, just greenfield adoption
- **Sticky price point:** $390/month is low enough to clear a solo decision-maker budget threshold at most small clinics, reducing sales cycle friction
- **Network effects within local referral clusters:** Vets in the same region regularly refer to each other; one satisfied clinic can seed adjacent ones — Assumption: referral conversion rate is TBD and should be tracked from day one
- **Regulatory tailwinds:** Assumption: any future digital-record mandates (jurisdiction-specific) could accelerate adoption — PM to confirm whether such regulation exists or is proposed
- **Expansion optionality:** Once SAM is penetrated domestically, the same model is portable to other English-speaking or similarly structured vet markets — not modeled here but should be a board-level signal

---

## Market Timing

- **Favorable entry window:** The 70% unserved figure (if validated) suggests the market is pre-consolidation — early movers can build switching-cost moats through data lock-in and workflow integration before a well-funded competitor enters
- **Risk of waiting:** If a broader veterinary practice-management suite adds scheduling as a module, the unserved 70% shrinks rapidly
- **Target go-to-market launch:** TBD — PM should define a launch date and work backward from the 434-clinic SOM target to set quarterly milestones
- **Break-even signal:** At $390/clinic/month, Target: ~130 clinics cover a $50,000/month cost base (Assumption: placeholder cost base — PM to confirm actual burn rate)

---

## Gaps & Risks

| Gap | Impact | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 70% unserved figure is an estimate | SAM could be ±30% | Run a 50-clinic survey or sales-team audit |
| CRM covers only Fernway's known contacts | TAM may be understated if 6,200 is not exhaustive | Cross-check with a vet licensing registry (if publicly available in-country) |
| No churn data | SOM Year 3 ARR could be significantly lower | Instrument early pilots for 3-month and 12-month retention |
| No sales-capacity data | 434-clinic target may be physically unachievable with current headcount | Model ramp by sales rep and define hiring plan |
| Pricing not tested at this segment | $390 may face resistance or may be underpriced | Run a willingness-to-pay test with 10–15 prospects |
| No competitive landscape data provided | SAM erosion risk is unquantified | Map direct and adjacent competitors before board presentation |

---

## Next Steps

1. **Validate the 70% unserved estimate** — run a structured 30-clinic outreach or internal sales-team audit within the next 2 weeks; this single figure moves SAM by up to $5.8M
2. **Confirm the total clinic count** — verify whether Fernway's CRM of 6,200 is exhaustive or a subset; cross-reference with any publicly available vet licensing data in-country
3. **Define the sales-capacity model** — map current headcount to a realistic clinic-per-rep-per-quarter figure; use it to stress-test the 434-clinic SOM target
4. **Instrument churn from pilot day one** — even a 5% monthly churn erodes the SOM materially; set up tracking before the first paid customer goes live
5. **Run a willingness-to-pay test** — present the $390 price to 10–15 unserved prospects and record objections; adjust SOM sensitivity bands before the board meeting
6. **Map the competitive landscape** — identify any scheduling tools already sold into adjacent vet segments to quantify SAM erosion risk; deliver findings alongside this document
